correctness.rationale: The Chebyshev recurrence yields T_j(A)=(S^j+S^−j)/2. In the sign quadratic form, each summand z_a z_(a+j) has mean zero for 1≤j<n, and its product with another summand has mean one exactly if the unordered index pairs match. Equal orientations account for n matches if j=k, opposite orientations another n if j+k=n; these are disjoint matches even at j=k=n/2. Each separated distinct alias pair removes 2nr^n from the shared-probe variance; the lower member j of such a pair ranges from 1 to min(k,n−1−k,floor((n−1)/2)). On C4 the variances are (4r²,8r⁴+4r⁶) and (4r²+8r⁴,4r⁶); positive variances and costs ensure a unique positive real allocation by equality in the stated Cauchy–Schwarz bound. The difference of optimized variance–work products has the sign of the stated Δ. In x=r² I independently reconstructed the sextic P(√x), ran rational Sturm with variations 5 and 1 at x=0,1 and a nonzero constant last term, and found exactly one simple root in each squared bracket. Sign agreement of R and U retains only the second and fourth roots. This test is sufficient: the first squaring is reversible because U+2√3 x√(2+4x)=1+x(2√3√(2+4x)−2)>0. Independent exact sign bounds at r=1/100, 1/2 and 99/100 give +,−,+, yielding the displayed strict phases. Rational bisection confirms 0.237180713823998328… and 0.809548040154000412…. Independent exhaustive sign-vector calculations corroborated the covariance and every admissible cutoff at r=2/3 on orders 3 through 8. This proves only the two-block continuous allocation result under the specified one-sided recurrence costs.
residual_risks: The two-probe versus shared-probe variance comparison is not an equal-budget comparison. Neither the continuous optimum nor its two switches is asserted for integral budgets, different cost models, or implementations exploiting T_1=T_3.

value.rationale: The exact covariance identifies when ignoring cross-degree terms is valid and when it misses an entire positive alias pair. The smallest cycle with two possible nonempty degree cutoffs already exhibits a twice-reversing choice, an exact counterexample to monotonic cutoff selection as coefficient decay changes in a standard continuous allocation model. The thresholds describe the full phase diagram, not small numerical gains or an unmotivated instance.
